experiments.scope: One 8-bit modular addition; all 65536 ordered input pairs enumerated exhaustively by the organizer evaluator.
experiments.hypothesis: Flipping the most significant bit of one addend changes the sum in exactly the most significant bit: output XOR difference 0x80 with exact probability 1 (65536/65536). This is the carry-free sign-bit transition used throughout Wang-style SHA-1 path analysis.

experiments.scope: One 8-bit modular addition; all 65536 ordered input pairs enumerated exhaustively by the organizer evaluator.
experiments.hypothesis: Flipping the least significant bit of one addend yields an LSB-only output XOR difference 0x01 with exact probability 1/2 (32768/65536): the canonical carry-propagation transition of the path probability calculus.

experiments.scope: One 8-bit modular addition; all 65536 ordered input pairs enumerated exhaustively by the organizer evaluator.
experiments.hypothesis: Flipping the most significant bit of both addends yields zero output XOR difference with exact probability 1 (65536/65536): the two sign-bit carries cancel modulo 2^8.

experiments.scope: One 8-bit modular addition; all 65536 ordered input pairs enumerated exhaustively by the organizer evaluator.
experiments.hypothesis: Flipping the low two bits of one addend yields an LSB-only output XOR difference 0x01 with exact probability 1/4 (16384/65536): a two-step carry-propagation check of the same calculus.
